# Herdr selection list: gate background/foreground sync on DB-update check before spawning wl commands

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list spawns a burst of `wl` CLI processes on a fixed cadence — background `wl sync` every 60s plus a full refresh (`wl next`, 2× `wl list` mandatory subsets, expanded-children fetches) on every 30s auto-refresh tick — **regardless of whether the worklog database changed**. When the pane is idle (no agents writing, no remote activity), each cycle wastes 3–5 process spawns and a full git sync round-trip for zero visible change.

## Users

- **Herdr users running the selection list with auto-refresh/auto-sync on** — want the list to stay current without constant background `wl` process churn (spawn overhead, git fetch/pull/merge/push, lock contention with other panes).
- **Multi-pane / multi-agent setups** — the reduction in unnecessary `wl sync` invocations reduces lock-storm pressure between panes and cross-process DB churn.

Example user stories:
- As a Herdr user with an idle backlog, I want the selection list to avoid spawning any `wl` commands when nothing changed, so my machine isn't churning processes and git round-trips every 30–60s.
- As a Herdr user, I want background sync to still run at least once per configurable window (default 60s) even when nothing changed locally, so I still receive remote changes pushed by other machines.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On an auto-refresh tick, when the worklog DB has not changed since the last refresh cycle, the pane spawns **zero** `wl` processes for that tick (no `wl next`, no `wl list`, no children fetches, no `wl sync`, no action-count fetch).
2. On an auto-sync tick, `wl sync` is skipped when (a) the DB has not changed since the last cycle **and** (b) the last successful sync is fresher than the configurable max-staleness cap (default 60s). If either condition fails, the sync runs (subject to the existing heartbeat / single-flight / `--if-idle` guards).
3. The max-staleness cap is configurable via the Herdr settings file (e.g. new `maxSyncStalenessMs` setting, default `60000`), clamped to a sane minimum like the sync interval clamp.
4. Manual user actions — `S` (sync) and `r` (refresh) keypresses — always run, ignoring the gate.
5. The very first cycle after pane start always runs (no prior "last seen" signal), and any failure to read the DB-change signal fails **open** (the cycle runs), so the list can never go stale due to a signal-read error.
6. The existing cross-instance heartbeat (`last-sync-time`), single-flight, and `--if-idle` guards remain in place for syncs that do run.
7. Unit tests cover: gate skip/run decisions for refresh and sync ticks (changed/unchanged DB, stale/fresh last-sync, manual override, first-cycle, fail-open), plus the new setting's parse/clamp behavior.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The Herdr plugin package (`packages/herdr`) has **zero npm dependencies** and intentionally duplicates small shared helpers per TUI (decision Q2c in WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B) — a small pure helper duplicating the counter-read logic is consistent with this pattern.
- The DB-change signal must be cheap (a file read or two) and must NOT spawn a `wl` process itself — that is the whole point of the gate.
- The signal must be cross-process stable: the wl CLI read cache (F2) deliberately avoids SQLite file mtimes because "the SQLite files are rewritten by the app on every open/close cycle… file-based fingerprints are not stable across processes" (`src/read-cache.ts`). The gate must not produce false "changed" signals from the pane's own reads.
- Do not change wl CLI sync behavior itself; the incremental-sync work (WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q) is separate scope.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `runWorklistTui` registers two scheduler tasks: `refresh` (every `refreshIntervalMs`, default 30s, always calls `doRefresh(false)` → spawns read commands) and `sync` (every `syncIntervalMs`, default 60s, calls `doSync(true, heartbeatTtlMs)` then `doRefresh(false)`). Plus a `resume-poll` task that calls `doRefresh(true)` on hidden→visible transition.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — `runSync` spawns `wl sync` fire-and-forget with cross-instance heartbeat skip (`last-sync-time` marker, `isSyncHeartbeatFresh`), single-flight guard, and `--if-idle`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — all read commands (`wl next`, `wl list`, children, action-count) go through `runWl`; the CLI serves many from its on-disk read cache (F2), but a process spawn still occurs per command.
- `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — the wl CLI maintains a monotonic per-worklog-dir **state counter** (`~/.cache/wl/state/<sha256(worklogDir)>.json`, `{ "state": N }`), bumped by every wl write command and by post-sync invalidation (`invalidateCacheForWrite`). This is the natural "DB changed" signal: cross-process, stable across reads, and already the CLI's freshness authority.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — typed settings JSON with clamped intervals; `syncIntervalMs` has a 60s minimum clamp.
- Manual `S`/`r` keypresses dispatch to `doSync()` / `doRefresh(true)` unconditionally.

## Desired change

- Add a small pure module in `packages/herdr` (e.g. `db-change.ts`) that:
  - resolves the wl cache dir (mirroring `resolveCacheDir()` precedence: `WL_CACHE_DIR` → `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/wl` → `~/.cache/wl`);
  - reads the state counter for the resolved worklog dir (`state/<sha256(worklogDir)>.json`), returning the counter value (0 when absent); and
  - exposes a `DbChangeTracker`/helper that remembers the last-seen counter per pane and answers `dbChangedSinceLastCycle()` (fail-open: any read error ⇒ true).
- Gate the scheduler tasks in `runWorklistTui`:
  - `refresh` tick: skip (spawn nothing) when the DB is unchanged since the last cycle.
  - `sync` tick: skip `wl sync` when DB unchanged **and** last successful sync (heartbeat marker) is within the configurable max-staleness cap; otherwise run `doSync` + `doRefresh` as today.
  - `resume-poll` hidden→visible transition: apply the same DB-change gate (list content is identical when nothing changed).
  - Manual `S`/`r` paths unchanged (always run).
- Add the configurable cap to settings (e.g. `maxSyncStalenessMs`, default 60s, clamped ≥1s or aligned with the sync-interval clamp) and pass it through `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`.
- Keep all existing guards (heartbeat, single-flight, `--if-idle`) for syncs that do run.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts` — NEW: pure DB-change signal reader (wl cache-dir resolution + state-counter read + last-seen tracker), fail-open.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — expose/adapt staleness helpers (reuse `readSyncHeartbeatMs`) so the sync tick can decide "DB unchanged AND sync fresh ⇒ skip".
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — wire the gate into the `refresh` / `sync` / `resume-poll` scheduler tasks; manual `S`/`r` untouched.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — new `maxSyncStalenessMs` setting (default `60000`) with clamping.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass the new setting into `runWorklistTui`.
- `src/read-cache.ts` — read-only reference for the counter-file format/path derivation (no changes expected).
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/db-change.test.ts` (NEW), plus updates to `auto-sync.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts`.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W` — Cross-instance sync heartbeat (F3): the `last-sync-time` marker and heartbeat TTL this change composes with. Completed.
- `WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E` — wl sync lock storm: auto-sync single-flight / `--if-idle` guards; gating reduces spawn pressure further. Completed.
- `WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA` — wl CLI read cache (F2) with the state-counter fingerprint this gate reuses as its signal. Completed.
- `WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q` — Incremental sync: only export/push changed work items (CLI-side; explicitly out of scope here). Open.
- `WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B` — Smart-selection duplication decision (Q2c): precedent for duplicating a small pure helper into the Herdr package. Completed.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — release workflow (no code impact; doc reference).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Remote-pull latency (accepted tradeoff, user-confirmed):** skipping `wl sync` when the DB is unchanged delays pulling remote changes until the next sync that does run. Bounded by the max-staleness cap (default 60s) so remote freshness is never worse than the cap.
- **Signal completeness:** the state counter is bumped by wl CLI writes and post-sync invalidation. External tools writing the SQLite DB directly (not via wl) would not bump it — mitigated by the staleness cap, which forces a periodic sync regardless. Assumed acceptable.
- **Configurable cap naming/units:** `maxSyncStalenessMs` in ms, default 60000, clamped to ≥1s (aligned with `heartbeatTtlForInterval`'s clamp) — exact name subject to implementer/plan review.
- **Scope-creep guard:** incremental sync (WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q), event-driven window subscription (WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ), and WAL checkpointing (WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I) are tracked separately and must NOT be pulled into this work item.
- **Behavioral parity:** when the DB IS changing, cadence must match today (no additional latency); only the no-change case adds skipping.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (asked 2026-08-07): "If the local DB hasn't changed, should the background `wl sync` also be skipped? That means remote changes pushed by other machines would only be pulled when local activity bumps the counter (or via manual `S`). Acceptable — or should the sync path stay ungated while only the refresh reads are skipped?" — Answer (user): "Partially acceptable. wl sync can be skipped if no local DB changes. However, it should not go more than 1 minute (configurable) without being run." Source: interactive reply. → Implemented as AC2/AC3: sync is gated by (DB unchanged AND last successful sync within configurable max-staleness cap, default 60s).
- Q2 (asked 2026-08-07): "Should manual refresh (`r`) and manual sync (`S`) always run regardless of the check? (My assumption: yes — user-initiated actions always execute.)" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply. → Implemented as AC4.
- Q3 (asked 2026-08-07, /skill:find-related): "Which work items are related?" — Research: the find-related script (`find_related.py --work-item-id WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ`) resolved the wrong worklog store (SorraAgents framework repo) on both runs and returned unrelated items (OpenBrain submission, file-path convention, a-y shortcut). The matches were excluded per the skill's conservative policy (false negatives preferred); the curated Related work section above (verified via `wl show` against the ContextHub store) is authoritative.
data.title: Herdr selection list: gate background/foreground sync on DB-update check before spawning wl commands

## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.
data.title: Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item

## Problem

`wl doctor prune --days N` hard-deletes items locally, but the next `wl sync` re-adds them all from the remote ref, because `mergeWorkItems` (src/sync.ts) re-imports every remote item missing locally (`if (!localItem) { mergedMap.set(remoteItem.id, remoteItem); }`). There is no `--no-pull` and prune has no push/rewrite path.

## Observed (2026-08-13)

- Ran `wl doctor prune --days 0` → 1,034 items hard-deleted locally (2941 → 1907 items)
- Ran `wl sync` → 'Work items added: 1034' — all resurrected from `refs/worklog/data` (back to 2941)
- Net result: prune is a no-op in a synced setup; items remain soft-deleted forever (the 'deleted but not pruned' backlog)

## Proposed fix

Add `--push` (or auto-push) to `wl doctor prune` that, after hard-deleting locally, rewrites the remote worklog ref with the pruned local state — mirroring `doctor foreign-items --apply --push` which already uses `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (src/sync.ts:1130).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl doctor prune --days N --push` leaves the remote ref without the pruned items
- [ ] A subsequent `wl sync` does NOT resurrect the pruned items
- [ ] `--dry-run` unchanged; default remains no-push (safe)
- [ ] Unit/integration test covers prune+push against a temp git repo
data.title: wl doctor prune cannot persist: sync re-adds pruned items from remote ref

# Write unit tests for auto-downgrade of critical priority

## Goal
Add comprehensive unit tests covering the auto-downgrade behavior for critical priority items transitioning to terminal states.

## Test Coverage Required

Per Acceptance Criteria 4 of parent (WL-0MSJM4EIV001A0V9):

1. **`wl update --status completed`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
2. **`wl update --stage in_review`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
3. **`wl close`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
4. **No-op: non-critical priorities** — verify high/medium/low unchanged on terminal transition
5. **No-op: non-terminal transitions** — verify critical priority unchanged when moving between non-terminal stages (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`)

## Implementation Notes

- Tests should use the existing test infrastructure (see `tests/database.test.ts` and `tests/cli/`)
- Follow the existing test patterns for `cascadePriorityDowngrade` tests
- Tests should verify both the priority change AND the reporting output (AC3 of parent)
- Consider both JSON and human-readable output paths

### Key Files
- `tests/database.test.ts` — database layer tests
- `tests/cli/` — CLI command tests (update, close)

As an operator, I do not want the herdr downtime worker to inhibit dispatch based on the GLOBAL active_query signal when the proxy serves the local-only signal, so that remote/cloud streams never block local downtime dispatch. The backward-compatibility fallback to the global `active_query` for pre-fix proxies must be removed.

## Background

- `isIdleStatus`/`globalIdleChecks` in packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts: `const queryActive = status.local_active_query !== undefined ? status.local_active_query : status.active_query;` — the fallback to `active_query` exists for proxies that predate the `local_active_queries` counter (LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR, delivered in WL-0MSL2ZQIF006QB4Q).
- The global `active_query` is true whenever ANY request is in flight — local AND remote provider streams. Remote streams keep it true while the local model is idle with free slots, so the fallback can block legitimate downtime dispatch (RCA WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7).
- The local-only signal (`local_active_query`) is the correct busy signal for the local model.

## Design notes

- Remove the `local_active_query !== undefined ? ... : active_query` fallback; use only `local_active_query`.
- Fail-closed question to resolve: is a MISSING `local_active_query` now treated as busy (no dispatch) or idle (dispatch)? Decision: treat a missing signal as busy (fail-closed, consistent with the rest of the worker) — a pre-fix proxy must not cause dispatch on an unverifiable signal.
- parseLlamaStatus currently accepts an absent `local_active_query` (`undefined`); a work item must decide whether absence becomes null (busy) or a documented explicit non-dispatch.
- Update parseLlamaStatus doc + isIdleStatus/globalIdleChecks comments (LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR reference).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `globalIdleChecks` uses ONLY `local_active_query` once present in the payload; the `active_query` fallback is removed.
2. A payload WITHOUT `local_active_query` fails closed: the worker treats the status as busy (no dispatch) and the behaviour is documented — no silent degraded dispatch on pre-fix proxies.
3. Remote/cloud streams (global active_query true, local false) are never a dispatch inhibitor.
4. Test suite covers: local_active_query present (both values), local_active_query absent (busy), and the removal of the fallback branch.
data.title: Downtime idle detection: remove fallback to global active_query when local_active_query absent (fail-closed busy)

# Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches during cheap mode (use both local slots)

## Problem statement

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap-mode window (2026-08-22 report, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`) shows the local Qwen3 model busy only ~25-38% of the window. Root cause is structural, not demand: the downtime worker dispatches strictly **single-flight** (one work item at a time, WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY), each dispatched session consumes exactly **one** local slot, and cheap mode provides **two** slots. The second cheap slot is essentially never used, and the per-item tail (agent tool-execution gaps between generation bursts, 10s-5min each) is pure idle that nothing else can fill.

24 herdr `audit-WL-*` sessions ran nearly sequentially: short generation bursts (3-10s) separated by long tool-execution gaps. Inter-run scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn) added another ~70s per dispatch cycle.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — pays for remote fallback tokens; wants maximum value from the always-on local iGPU during cheap hours (01:00-10:00).
- **Herdr downtime users** — want more audits/work items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During cheap mode, the downtime worker MAY dispatch a second work item to fill an otherwise-idle second local slot, subject to a bounded concurrency cap (start with 2 concurrent dispatches).
2. Dispatch of the second item respects the same idle-gate contract (requires `requiredFreeSlots` free slots observed for the idle-threshold duration) — it must NOT queue or dispatch into a busy slot.
3. The concurrency cap is configurable via downtime settings (default 1 = current behavior, so fast/operator-interactive mode is unchanged unless explicitly enabled).
4. Fast mode (3 slots) and operator-interactive sessions keep priority: downtime never displaces an active operator session slot; only genuinely free slots are used.
5. Tests: bounded-concurrency dispatch logic (cap honored, second dispatch only fires when ≥1 slot free for N polls), no regression to existing single-flight claim safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
6. Measured outcome: nightly cheap-window busy % for the local model increases vs. baseline (target ≥ 2x the current ~25-38%).

## Notes

- Coupling: dispatched audits run `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`, so ONE audit uses at most 1 slot (parent then child serially). Two concurrent audits therefore use at most 2 slots = exactly cheap mode's capacity (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS). Raising fan-out (see the AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM item) changes this budget and must be coordinated — total in-flight local streams must not exceed the cheap pool.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (audit fan-out bound), WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY (single-flight dispatch), WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (referenced in code comments, not found in worklog — verify against per-slot idle tracker).
- The 04:00-06:00 evidence (24 sessions, 252 local streams, 48% idle stream-level) is in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` and the analysis session log.
data.title: Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches (use both cheap-mode slots)

## Problem

When the proxy returns a 503 'All providers exhausted' response (from proxy/provider.py _build_exhausted_response), the Worklog recovery extension's classifyError() function does not match this error against any of its 8 categories (RATE_LIMIT, SERVER_ERROR, AUTH_ERROR, CONTEXT_LENGTH, QUOTA_EXHAUSTED, TIMEOUT, TERMINATED, PARSE_ERROR). The result is ErrorCategory.UNKNOWN, which triggers:

  Unrecognized error: All providers exhausted

...and **halts the session with no retry**. The agent stalls waiting for user intervention.

## Solution

Add 'All providers exhausted' to the SERVER_ERROR category patterns so the existing retry loop (triggerInvisibleContinue with exponential backoff) picks it up. The error message contains no HTTP status digits or standard error keywords that the current patterns match against.

### File to modify

ContextHub/packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts

Add to DEFAULT_SERVER_ERROR_PATTERNS:

  /all providers exhausted/i,
  /no provider available/i,

### Optional enhancement (future)

If the proxy emits a Retry-After HTTP header or the Worklog extension gains access to it (from the JSON body), the retry loop could use that value as the initial backoff delay instead of the default 2-second baseDelayMs.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Error message 'All providers exhausted' is classified as ErrorCategory.SERVER_ERROR (not UNKNOWN).
2. The Worklog recovery module triggers triggerInvisibleContinue() for this error (same path as existing SERVER_ERROR).
3. The retry loop performs exponential backoff and auto-continues when providers become available.
4. No regression: existing patterns still match their expected categories.
5. Tests for error-patterns.ts pass.
data.title: Classify 'All providers exhausted' for automatic retry

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime worker audit tier selects a candidate via `selectAuditCandidate` (freshness checked at selection time), then `dispatchClaimedTier` runs CAS claim → `recordDispatch` (writes the "Auto-dispatched…" work-item comment + rolling marker) → spawn. If **during the interim** — between selection and the comment/spawn — a valid audit was recorded (e.g. a human or another process ran `wl audit-set`), the worker still writes the dispatch comment and spawns a redundant audit pane. The stale/unaudited state it selected no longer exists, so the dispatch is wasted work and the comment is misleading.

Observed (WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B): dispatch comment + marker written at 2026-08-24T20:51:49Z while a valid audit existed/landed; a later comment then made the audit appear stale and the item was re-dispatched repeatedly (audit re-recorded 2026-08-25T09:56Z).

RCA: `claimItem` CAS-guards status/stage only (TIER_EXPECTED audit = completed/in_review) — a manual `wl audit-set` does NOT change status/stage, so the claim still succeeds. There is no freshness re-check between selection and `recordDispatch`/spawn. Discovered-from: WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B.

## Desired change

In the audit-tier dispatch path, after selecting a candidate and before writing the dispatch comment/marker and spawning, re-check that the item still lacks a fresh audit (`isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` from @worklog/shared/icons). If a fresh audit now exists:
- skip the dispatch entirely (no comment, no marker, no spawn) and fall through to the next tier — treat as "already audited", not "no-candidate"/cooldown and not a strike;
- on a failed spawn (`recordDispatchFailure` / spawn-failed path), do not record/comment a failure trace if a valid audit was recorded during the interim — the pane is moot, not a failure to log as such.

Mirror the same interim freshness re-check in any other dispatcher that comments on audit dispatch (heartbeat does not comment; it invokes the runner directly — verify).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Integration test: select a stale/un-audited candidate, then record a valid audit in the "interim", then verify dispatch downgrades to a no-op (no item comment, no rolling-log `kind=audit` marker, no spawn) and falls through to the next tier without triggering the no-candidate cooldown
- [ ] Integration test: spawn-failure trace (`outcome: spawn-failed`) is NOT appended (and no failure comment) when a valid audit was recorded during the interim
- [ ] A genuinely unaudited item still dispatches exactly as today (comment + marker + spawn)
- [ ] Convention/naming: the interim check is a single dep on the worker boundary (e.g. a `hasFreshAudit(itemId)` dep) so it is testable without wl
- [ ] Full project test suite passes

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchClaimedTier` / audit-tier dispatch in `dispatchDowntimeWork` (~lines 1854–1904), `selectAuditCandidate` (~3020), worker deps (~879)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire the interim freshness dep into `createDowntimeDeps` (alongside `getNextAuditCandidate`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — interim-freshness integration tests

## Related work

- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — audit tier dispatch
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY — dispatched-marker exclusion
- WL-0MT3PHW4I002SNOV — active-audit single-flight
- WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B — observed stale-audit loop (discovered-from)
data.title: Herdr audit tier: re-check for a fresh audit after selection, before claim/comment/spawn

## Problem statement

Two coupled defects leave valid audits visible as stale ("out of date audit"):

1. **Comment bumps invalidate audits.** `wl comment add` → `createComment` → `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` (packages/shared/src/database.ts:3282, persistent-store `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` ~3416) advances the work item `updatedAt` for ANY comment. `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (packages/shared/src/icons.ts:269) compares `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`; a comment added after the audit (e.g. "Audit re-evaluation (forced --force)" on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B at 21:26:17Z vs audit 21:21:03Z) therefore flips the audit to stale ⏳ even though no content changed. The documented guarantee in icons.ts ("Flag-only flips of needsProducerReview do not move updatedAt, so a previously valid audit remains fresh") does NOT cover comments — comments are the common case that breaks it.

2. **Audit persistence does not atomically update auditedAt.** `wl audit-set` (src/commands/audit-result.ts) writes the `audit_results` row (auditedAt = now) but does not touch the work item; `wl update --audit-text` (src/commands/update.ts) also only writes `saveAuditResult`. There is no single atomic operation that both records the audit AND refreshes the freshness clock, so a comment between audit and display (or a re-evaluation that comments instead of persisting — see WL-0MT8KT2LO0056KLF) leaves the record behind `updatedAt`.

Investigation outcome — audit-content comments can be removed (no consumer parses them):
- implement skill: reads the audit **record** (`/skill:audit` → runner → `wl audit-show`; `audit_report_<id>.md`); comments are only generic context in Step 4 ("pay attention to comments"), never parsed as verdicts
- ship skill `check-audit-gate.js`: `wl audit-show` → `readyToClose`/`rawOutput`/`summary`; `wl comment add` is used only to WRITE merge logs
- heartbeat, report skill, herdr TUI (`worklist.ts`, icons): all read `auditResult`/`auditedAt` from the record

So the audit verdict must live in the audit record only; audits duplicated in comments are dead weight and actively harmful (they bump updatedAt).

Discovered-from: WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B.

## Desired change

1. **Freshness clock:** make audit freshness reflect content-only changes. Options to evaluate (pick one, document trade-offs):
   a. exclude comments (and `needsProducerReview` flag flips, already excluded) from `updatedAt` bumps via `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt`; or
   b. `isAuditFresh` uses a content/activity fingerprint rather than `updatedAt`; or
   c. `wl audit-set`/`--audit-text` perform an atomic "record audit + set updatedAt = auditedAt" so a later comment still breaks it (not fully fixing) — likely insufficient alone.
2. **Atomic audit persistence:** `wl audit-set` (and/or `wl update --audit-text`) should be a single operation that records the `audit_results` row and refreshes the item's freshness marker so "audit recorded" always implies "audit fresh" immediately.
3. **Remove audit-content comments:** stop adding the audit report/verdict to work-item comments (the verdict lives in the audit record). Keep comments for dispatches/trails (herdr "Auto-dispatched…" is a dispatch marker, not audit content — out of scope) and for human annotations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a post-audit comment is added, the audit remains fresh: `wl show <id> --json` + a comment → `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` stays true; TUI keeps the passed icon, not ⏳ (add a regression test in packages/shared tests for the chosen mechanism)
- [ ] `wl audit-set` is atomic: after it, `auditedAt >= updatedAt` immediately (no intermediate window where a read shows stale) — or the alternative chosen mechanism guarantees the same
- [ ] The audit report/verdict is no longer duplicated into work-item comments by audit flows; existing duplicated comments on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B are documented as legacy (no migration required unless trivially safe)
- [ ] Unit tests cover: comment-after-audit keeps fresh; audit-then-comment ordering matches the chosen freshness clock; `wl update --audit-text` path behaves identically to `wl audit-set`
- [ ] Docs updated: icons.ts guarantee comment, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md (or equivalent), audit SKILL.md where it describes the audit record as canonical
- [ ] Full project test suite passes

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh`, `stageDisplayIcon` (the ⏳ stale-passed path)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `createComment`/`touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` (~3246, 3416)
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` — `wl audit-set` (atomic auditedAt write)
- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--audit-text` persistence path
- `src/commands/comment.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — comment updatedAt semantics
- `packages/shared/src/icons.test.ts` (or equivalent) — freshness regression tests

## Related work

- WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B — observed stale audit (discovered-from)
- WL-0MT8KSTOE00871E7 — herdr interim freshness re-check (sibling)
- WL-0MT8KT2LO0056KLF — forced re-evaluation must persist (sibling; comment-only re-eval is the trigger that exposed this)
- WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R — flag-only flips do not move updatedAt (docs this gap for the needsProducerReview case)
data.title: Audit freshness: keep audit valid after post-audit comments; persist auditedAt atomically; remove audit-content comments

## Summary

Write the unit tests that pin the gate skip/run decisions and the new setting's parse/clamp behavior before implementation (test-first, TDD contract).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New `packages/herdr/src/db-change.test.ts` covers:
   - Cache-dir resolution precedence: `WL_CACHE_DIR` → `/wl` → `~/.cache/wl`

   - Fail-open on signal-read error (cycle runs)
4. `auto-sync.test.ts` covers the exposed staleness helper (last-sync age vs cap) if adapted from `readSyncHeartbeatMs`
5. All tests pass via the project test runner (`pnpm test`).

## Goal

Verify and strengthen `wl close` multi-id batch mode so that ship-skill-style callers can close N work items with a single `wl close <id1> <id2> ... --force --reason 'Shipped in v1.2.3'` call, receiving a clean JSON summary with per-item success/failure counts.

## Why

`wl close` already accepts `<ids...>` (multiple IDs) and processes them in a for loop (close.ts, action handler). However, the ship skill's closeWorkItemsAfterRelease (run-release.js) currently invokes `wl close` once per item (N subprocess forks for N items). The multi-id path exists but needs verification that: (a) `--force --reason` are applied uniformly across all IDs, (b) JSON output aggregates per-item results clearly, (c) errors on one item don't prevent closing others.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl close <id1> <id2> <id3> --force --reason "Shipped in v1.2.3" --json` closes all three items in one subprocess call, with each item's success/error reported in a JSON array.
2. `--force` is applied to every ID uniformly; `--reason` is stored as a comment on every item.
3. Errors on one item do not abort the batch (per-item error isolation, consistent with current loop behavior).
4. JSON output has a clear top-level structure: `{ results: [{ id, success, error? }, ...], closed: N, failed: N }`.
5. Tests: unit tests in ContextHub's test suite cover multi-id close with --force --reason, partial failure, and JSON output structure.

## Key files

- src/commands/close.ts (action handler, for loop over ids, JSON output)
- tests/ (new multi-id close tests)

# Client-side compaction response to llm-proxy compaction gate

## Problem statement

The llm proxy's cheap-mode hard local-routing cap will return a **compaction gate** response (an informative 4xx) when a request's context exceeds the cap. Today no client understands this signal, so oversized cheap-mode sessions would stall — silently dropping, queue-fallback to expensive remote, or burning 10–26 minute near-full-slot prefills.

## Users

- **Cheap-mode session users** — When the proxy gates an oversized context, the client automatically compacts and retries without user intervention.
- **Session operators** — When a session cannot be compacted further, they receive explicit guidance (never a silent drop).

**User stories:**
- "As a cheap-mode user, when my request hits the proxy's compaction gate, I want the session to automatically compact and retry — I shouldn't see an error or be dropped."
- "As a session operator, if a session can't be compacted further, I want a clear error message explaining why and what to do next."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Gate detection** — The client detects the compaction gate response per a wire contract (HTTP status code + guidance header/body) and routes to the compaction flow, distinctly from `stopReason === "length"` handling. The exact shape (status code, header name, body format) is defined in this item and coordinated with the parallel llm-proxy item LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S.
2. **Client-side compaction** — Upon gate detection, the client runs compaction via the existing `/compact` machinery (reusing WL-0MR269PDV00970YP `executeCompactAndContinue()`) without user interaction.
3. **Auto-retry** — After compaction completes successfully, the original request is automatically retried (reusing the auto-continue pattern from WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O); the outcome is surfaced to the user.
4. **Non-compactable fallback** — If compaction fails or is unavailable, the client shows explicit guidance (never silently drops). A defined fallback is surfaced (e.g., "session cannot be compacted — consider starting a new session").
5. **Tests and docs** — Unit tests cover the detect → compact → retry flow; wire contract and behavior are documented (API/CONFIG docs); full test suite passes green.

## Constraints

- **Never silently drop** a gated request.
- **Never queue-fallback to remote** — that burns cost.
- **Never burn a near-full-slot prefill** (10–26 minute wait).
- Reuse existing compact-and-continue machinery; do not reimplement.
- The compaction gate is distinct from `stopReason === "length"` — they must not be conflated.
- Cheap-mode sessions only — the proxy gate is a cheap-mode signal.
- The wire contract must be finalized with the parallel llm-proxy item before implementation.

## Existing state

- **WL-0MR269PDV00970YP** — *Compact-and-Continue Handler* (completed): `executeCompactAndContinue()` in `recovery.ts` executes `/compact` and returns a `CompactContinueResult`; triggers via `hasContextLengthStop()` on `agent_end`.
- **WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O** — *Auto-continue after mid-session compaction* (completed): `shouldAutoContinueAfterCompaction()` and `shouldTriggerCompactionContinue()` in `recovery.ts`; handler in `register-recovery.ts`; safety guards (abort/mutex/session-generation) all in place.
- **`triggerInvisibleContinue()`** in `register-recovery.ts` — the retry-loop primitive used for CONTEXT_LENGTH and compaction continuations.
- Proxy side: `context_pressure` signal exists at 0.8×cap; the new compaction gate is at 1.0×cap (hard cap).

## Desired change

1. **Recovery module** — Add a new detection path that intercepts HTTP 4xx responses containing the compaction gate signal. Route to compaction via `executeCompactAndContinue()`.
2. **Retry loop** — After compaction, trigger the retry via the existing invisible-continue mechanism (the same `agent.prompt([])` pattern), reusing the auto-continue mutex and guard infrastructure.
3. **Fallback handler** — When compaction cannot succeed (compact itself errors, or session is already compacted to minimum), display explicit guidance and stop with a clear user message.
4. **Tests** — Unit tests covering: gate detection → compaction → retry; compaction failure → fallback; non-compactable session → explicit guidance.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/recovery.ts` — New gate-response detection function (e.g., `isCompactionGateResponse()`); gate-detection branch in the `agent_end` handler or request-intercept layer.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — Wire gate detection into the existing recovery dispatch; reuse `executeCompactAndContinue()` and `triggerInvisibleContinue()`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts` — Possibly extend `ContinuationState` to track "compaction gate retry" as a distinct retry category.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/compact-continue.test.ts` (or new file `compaction-gate.test.ts`) — Unit tests for gate detection, compact → retry, and fallback.
- `docs/` — API/CONFIG docs for the wire contract and client-side behavior.

## Related work

- **LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S** — *llm-proxy: cheap-mode hard local-routing cap* (parallel, not blocking) — emits the compaction gate signal. Wire contract coordination needed.
- **LP-0MTAQNAIH001RN1S** — *Evaluation/reporting* for the cheap-mode cap.
- **WL-0MR269PDV00970YP** — *Compact-and-Continue Handler* (completed, reuse target).
- **WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O** — *Auto-continue after mid-session compaction* (completed, reuse target).
- **WL-0MR5QR1790034LXA** — *Fix: Auto-continue after compaction for max output tokens* (completed, CONTEXT_LENGTH path).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Wire contract not finalized** — The compaction gate response shape (status, headers, body) depends on the parallel llm-proxy item LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S. Mitigation: implement with a configurable/extendable gate-detection interface so the contract can be pinned without rework.
- **Infinite retry loop** — If compaction does not reduce context enough to clear the cap, the detect → compact → retry cycle could loop. Mitigation: limit retry attempts (e.g., 2 retries) and fall back to explicit guidance after max retries.
- **Race with other recovery paths** — The gate-detection path must not race with CONTEXT_LENGTH (stopReason === "length") recovery or the auto-continue path. Mitigation: reuse existing `_continueInProgress` mutex and add a gate-specific retry category in `ContinuationState`.
- **HTTP response interception layer** — The gate signal arrives as an HTTP 4xx response; the exact interception point (fetch wrapper, agent request layer, or lower-level transport) must be identified. Mitigation: review existing HTTP error handling in the packages before implementing.
- **Assumption**: compaction after a gate retry uses the same continuation prompt and flow as CONTEXT_LENGTH. If different behavior is needed, the continuation logic must be parameterized.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What is the exact wire contract for the compaction gate response (status code, header name, body format)?" — Answer: **OPEN** — to be defined in coordination with the llm-proxy item LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S (parallel, not blocking). Suggested: HTTP 413 (Payload Too Large) with a `X-Compaction-Gate: true` header and a guidance body; final shape TBD with LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S author.
- Q2: "What constitutes 'non-compactable' and what fallback guidance is appropriate?" — Answer (assumption): Non-compactable = compact fails (error from /compact) or session is at minimum context size. Fallback = explicit error message: "Context cannot be compacted further — please start a new session to continue." Source: operator request; assumption recorded, confirming agent should validate during implementation.
- Q3: "Does the gate detection hook into the request/response layer (HTTP interceptor) or the agent_end handler?" — Answer (assumption): The gate is a proxy-level HTTP response (4xx), so detection belongs at the HTTP request/response layer, not `agent_end`. This is distinct from CONTEXT_LENGTH which is a model signal. Source: logical deduction from problem statement; confirming agent should verify implementation approach with operator.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`db-change.test.ts`** (NEW):
   1a. `resolveCacheDir()` precedence: `WL_CACHE_DIR` env overrides, falls back to `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/wl`, then `~/.cache/wl`.
   1b. `readStateCounter()` returns counter value from `<cacheDir>/state/<sha256(worklogDir)>.json` (0 when absent or unparseable).
   1c. `DbChangeTracker` first call with no prior value returns `changed=true`; subsequent calls return `changed=false` when counter unchanged.
   1d. `DbChangeTracker` returns `changed=true` (fail-open) on any read error (missing file, corrupt JSON, permission error).
2. **`worklist.test.ts`**:
   2a. Refresh tick: skips `doRefresh` when `dbChangedSinceLastCycle()` returns `false`; runs `doRefresh` when `true`.
   2b. Sync tick: skips `doSync`+`doRefresh` when DB unchanged AND heartbeat fresh within cap; runs when DB changed; runs when heartbeat stale beyond cap.
   2c. Manual `S` (sync) and `r` (refresh) always run, ignoring the gate.
   2d. First cycle after pane start always runs (no prior last-seen signal).
   2e. Fail-open: when `DbChangeTracker` read errors, the cycle runs.
3. **`settings.test.ts`**:
   3a. `maxSyncStalenessMs` defaults to `60000`.
   3b. `loadSettings` merges persisted value from JSON.
   3c. Out-of-range values are clamped (e.g., negative → default, values <1000ms → clamped to 1000ms, NaN/non-number → default).
4. All tests pass via `npm test` in `packages/herdr`.

## Minimal Implementation

- New `packages/herdr/src/db-change.test.ts` — mocks `fs.readFileSync` to test cache-dir resolution, state-counter read, and `DbChangeTracker` behavior.
- Extend `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — stub `doRefresh`/`doSync` and inject a controlled `DbChangeTracker`; test gate skip/run decisions for refresh/sync/manual/first-cycle/fail-open.
- Extend `packages/herdr/src/settings.test.ts` — test `maxSyncStalenessMs` in persisted settings, default value, clamp behavior.

## Dependencies

None — written first (TDD contract).
